title: seed_manifest

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI identifying the schema this seed manifest conforms to.

seed_manifest_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this seed manifest instance. Convention: {product-or-repo-slug}-seed-manifest. Examples: 'billing-api-seed-manifest', 'customer-portal-seed-manifest', 'devspec-toolkit-seed-manifest'. Should match the host repository name. Anti-pattern: 'seed-manifest-v1' (too generic) or using a version suffix here — version the manifest via the 'version' field.

version.description: SemVer string (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for the seed manifest format. Increment MINOR when adding new seeds; increment MAJOR for breaking structural changes.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when this seed manifest was initially created. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the most recent modification to this manifest. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Update whenever seeds or step_requirements change.

global_seed_order.description: Ordered list of seed IDs that AI prompts should read before generating any spec artifact. The order determines the precedence of context: earlier seeds provide foundational context, later seeds provide specifics. All prompts read seeds in this order via the 'Seed Order & Mandatory Sources' section. Should include at minimum the IDs for seed_overview.md and seed_tech_stack.md.

seed_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this seed document. Should match a corresponding entry in global_seed_order and/or step_requirements (validated by seed-lint). Example: 'seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack'. Convention: use the filename stem in kebab-case.

path.description: File path to the seed document relative to the repository root. Example: 'seed/seed_overview.md'.

description.description: What this seed file contains. Helps prompts understand whether to prioritize this seed for their step. Write from the prompt's perspective: what will it learn from this seed? Example: 'High-level product overview, goals, and user personas. Read first for all steps.' Avoid vague summaries like 'overview doc'.

required.description: Whether this seed document must be present for pipeline execution. true: pipeline will error if this file is missing. false: seed is optional and prompts may skip it when absent.

source_type.description: Category of the seed source. 'doc': narrative documentation (PRDs, meeting notes, design docs) — prose documents that are human-readable only. 'spec': formal specification or schema — JSON, YAML, or CSV files that can be parsed programmatically. 'config': project configuration or environment settings. 'other': any source not fitting the above categories. Values: 'narrative' describes prose documents like design briefs, user research reports, or meeting notes (human-readable only); 'structured' describes JSON, YAML, or CSV files that can be parsed programmatically; 'both' describes a Markdown document with embedded YAML front matter or structured tables (e.g., a spec guide with a machine-parseable requirements table). When a document is both narrative and machine-parseable, prefer 'spec' if it has a defined schema, or 'doc' if it is primarily human-authored prose. Anti-pattern: classifying a plaintext changelog as 'spec' or 'structured' — it must have a parseable format (JSON/YAML/CSV) to qualify.

hash.description: Optional SHA-256 content hash (64 hex chars) of the seed file at manifest-update time. Populated by `seed-index` tooling to let downstream validators detect whether a seed has changed since the manifest was last refreshed.

version.description: Optional version identifier for the seed document (semver like '1.2.0', a date like '2026-04-01', or a revision like 'rev-42'). Track this when the seed has an explicit author-maintained version. Distinct from `hash` — version is an author intent, hash is a verifiable content fingerprint.

items.description: Definition of a single seed document: its location, type, and role in the pipeline.

seeds.description: Registry of all seed files available for this project. Each entry describes a seed file's purpose and scope. Seeds are source-of-truth documents (PRDs, technical specs, meeting notes) that ground AI outputs in project reality. Must contain at least one entry; seed_ids here should align with global_seed_order and step_requirements values (validated by seed-lint).

^(\\d{2}[a-z]?)$.description: Array of seed IDs required for the pipeline step identified by the parent key. Each seed ID must match a seeds[*].seed_id value in this manifest. Example key-value pair: '04': ['seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack'] (FR list step requires both seeds). For multi-part steps use the full step key: '16a': ['seed-overview', 'seed-tech-stack', 'seed-domain-model']. Anti-pattern: key format '4' instead of '04' — step keys must be zero-padded two-digit strings, or the full step identifier for multi-part steps (e.g., '16a', '16b').

step_requirements.description: Mapping from pipeline step IDs to the seed files required by that step. Each step's AI prompt uses this to know which seed files to prioritize reading. Key: step ID matching the pattern NN or NNx (e.g., '04', '05', '16a'). Value: array of seed IDs from the seeds registry. Ensures each step gets the most relevant context without requiring all seeds. Steps not listed here fall back to reading global_seed_order.

doc_paths.description: Array of glob patterns identifying documentation files in the repository that the step_16 docs_impact validator monitors. Use forward-slash glob syntax relative to the repository root. Examples: ['docs/**/*.md', 'README.md', 'api-reference/**/*.yaml', 'guides/*.md']. Anti-pattern: absolute paths or OS-specific separators ('docs\*.md') — use forward-slash glob syntax only. Anti-pattern: listing individual files when a glob covers them ('README.md', 'SETUP.md' → use '*.md' at the root level instead).

description: Schema for the seed manifest defining seed documents, their ordering, and step requirements.
